correctness.rationale: For the original synchronous rule, neighboring differences inside a self-inclusive n-path evolve under the explicitly derived symmetric nonnegative tridiagonal matrix B_n. The normalized strictly positive Perron eigenvector gives exact differences λ_n^t y_i and span λ_n^t. Reflection forces common opinion limit 1/2. Internal confidence grows while its gaps shrink; the central confidence equals c0 δ^t up to first reception. The strict test yields no central reception exactly when δ<=λ_n and an exact floor-plus-one first reception clock otherwise. PF and the Rayleigh quotient rigorously give 0<λ_n<1, λ_n>=(n-2)/(n-1), enabling arbitrarily slow trust decay. The exact-rational six-vertex run and finite spectral simulations pass via verify.py but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The initiating work identifies analytically unresolved parameters controlling absent effective ties between equal-limit agents. The result answers that question exactly on a natural connected family, gives a sharp spectral boundary and finite first-reception clock, and proves permanent disappearance of a socially available tie for EVERY trust-decay parameter below one when block size can grow. It thereby separates reaching identical final beliefs from communicating along a physical edge at arbitrarily slow trust decay, not merely a small numerical refinement.
